Introduction Many international school students in Japan have their sights set on the elite Ivy League schools. The Ivy League refers to a group of eight private colleges and universities in the Northeastern United States. While the name “Ivy League” originally pertained to an athletic conference, over time it has come to represent overall academic excellence, selective admissions, historic traditions, and social prestige.The institutions within the Ivy League are:Brown UniversityColumbia UniversityCornell UniversityDartmouth CollegeHarvard UniversityUniversity of Pennsylvania (Penn)Princeton UniversityYale UniversityIn this blog, we’ll give a brief overview of each Ivy League school and summarize some key statistic most relevant to international students. Do you want to improve your chances of getting into a top-tier university? Schedule your consultation with Tokyo Academics today! Meet with Our Admissions Team The Ivy League Schools: What to KnowWhile these schools share the Ivy League designation and stand out for their high academic standards, each possesses unique qualities, cultures, and locations for prospective students to consider when making their decisions.Brown UniversityLocation: Providence, Rhode IslandFounded: 1764Known for its open curriculum, which allows students to design their own academic path, Brown promotes a learning environment where students explore and engage in diverse interests. Its diverse community, undergraduate research opportunities, and collaborations are some highlights.Columbia UniversityLocation: New York City, New YorkFounded: 1754Situated in the heart of Manhattan, Columbia offers rigorous academic programs and a core curriculum that ensures a broad-based education. Its location gives students unparalleled access to internships, cultural experiences, and more.Cornell UniversityLocation: Ithaca, New YorkFounded: 1865Located in upstate New York, Cornell combines rigorous academic programs with a commitment to public engagement. It boasts relatively more diverse academic programs than other Ivy League schools, from hotel administration to various engineering disciplines.Dartmouth CollegeLocation: Hanover, New HampshireFounded: 1769The smallest in the Ivy League, Dartmouth is known for its tight-knit community and emphasis on undergraduate education. The D-Plan, a unique quarter system (versus the standard semester system), offers students greater flexibility in their studies.Harvard UniversityLocation: Cambridge, MassachusettsFounded: 1636The oldest institution of higher education in the U.S., Harvard is renowned globally for its influence, rigorous academic programs, extensive library system, and emphasis on research. It is arguably the most well-renowned university worldwide.University of Pennsylvania (Penn)Location: Philadelphia, PennsylvaniaFounded: 1740Founded by Benjamin Franklin, Penn is recognized for integrating liberal arts and professional education. The Wharton School, Penn’s business school, is particularly renowned and often ranks as the highest-rated undergraduate business school in the United States.Princeton UniversityLocation: Princeton, New JerseyFounded: 1746Princeton is known for its commitment to undergraduate education, a strong emphasis on independent research, and a generous financial aid program. Students engage in independent projects, culminating in a senior thesis.Yale UniversityLocation: New Haven, ConnecticutFounded: 1701With its vast library system, diverse academic programs, and focus on research and global initiatives, Yale is committed to enriching the intellectual lives of its students. The residential college system fosters a strong sense of community.Non-Ivy League SchoolsOf course, other non-Ivy schools like MIT, Duke, and Stanford are equally reputable to the schools listed above and absolutely worth your consideration. While the Ivy League schools carry a strong brand name, students should ultimately pick the school best aligned with their goals and interests. Comparing the Ivy League SchoolsWhile the overall acceptance rate of the Ivy League schools is extremely low, it’s worth noting that international students are accepted at a higher rate. These schools all value having a diverse student body, meaning your unique experiences as an international school student can stand out.Below we’ve outlined the Ivy League rankings, share of international students, and more. In general, keep in mind the following factors considered by college admissions officers:Grade point average (GPA)Course selectionStandardized test scores (SAT, ACT, AP [Advanced Placement], IB [International Baccalaureate], etc.)Summer school / demonstrated interestResearch projects, publications, presentationsTeacher, counselor, or mentor recommendationsExtracurriculars, leadership, serviceEssays and interviewsFor further details, we recommend connecting with one of Tokyo Academics’ college admissions consultants who can work with you to plan your admissions journey.
